title: imap: X-USENET-IPFS-GET command — fetch arbitrary IPFS block by CID
description:
Why: IMAP clients that obtain a CID (from EMAILID via OBJECTID, from X-Usenet-IPFS-CID headers, or from any external source) have no way to retrieve the corresponding raw IPFS block through the IMAP interface. This command makes the IMAP server a gateway to the full IPFS network.

What:
Add X-USENET-IPFS-GET as a custom IMAP command.
- Syntax: <tag> X-USENET-IPFS-GET <cid-string>
- Untagged response on success delivers a synthetic RFC 5322 MIME message via IMAP literal:
    * X-USENET-IPFS-BLOCK {<byte-count>}
    From: ipfs-gateway@<configured hostname>
    Subject: IPFS:<cid>
    Message-ID: <<cid>@ipfs.local>
    X-Usenet-IPFS-CID: <cid>
    MIME-Version: 1.0
    Content-Type: application/octet-stream
    Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
    <blank line>
    <base64-encoded block bytes>
- Tagged completion:
    <tag> OK X-USENET-IPFS-GET completed
- Tagged failure responses:
    <tag> NO [NOTFOUND] CID not found
    <tag> BAD invalid CID syntax
- Advertise X-USENET-IPFS-GET in CAPABILITY.
- Valid in Authenticated and Selected states.

Although IMAP literals are binary-safe, wrapping in a synthetic RFC 5322 MIME message keeps the format consistent with NNTP XGET and JMAP blob download, and means the client receives a structured message it can parse with standard RFC 5322 tooling rather than an opaque byte stream.
notes: RESOLVED via JMAP: GET /jmap/download/{accountId}/{blobId}/{name} (crates/mail/src/blob.rs) already implements this. Validates blob_id as CID, fetches from IPFS via jmap.ipfs.get_raw_block(), wraps in synthetic RFC 5322 MIME message (same format this issue spec'd). Fully implemented with tests (400/403/404/503/500 cases). The IMAP X-command path remains blocked by imap-next library. This issue can be closed as superseded.
